newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end weaker after recent highs.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end weaker after recent highs.

text.p: Toronto stocks closed lower on Monday, retreating from recent highs, as weaker banks and oils outweighed rising golds and investors took profits.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index lost 24.69 points to close at 6467.41. Trading was moderate at 82.3 million shares worth C$1.3 billion ($935 million).
Earlier in the session, the index hit a new intra-session high of 6507.08 before being dampened by profit-taking in financial and energy issues.
"These things can't be going up forever," said ScotiaMcLeod director of trading Fred Ketchen.
Despite the losses, Ketchen forecast Toronto would roll higher. "This market still has got a lot of legs to it."
Nine of Toronto's 14 sub-groups ended higher, led by golds, consumer products and conglomerates. The weaker side included heavyweight oils, banks and transportation.
Declining issues led advancers 521 to 437, while 303 closed steady.
The tumble in energy issues was led by Abacan Resources Corp., after the Calgary, Alberta-based oil firm said its cash flow in 1997 and 1998 would be much lower than analysts' forecasts.
Abacan lost 62 percent of its value, falling 5.03 to 3.07 on more than 11 million shares.
Floor and wallcovering maker Domco Inc. soared after a takeover offer by U.S.-based Armstrong World Industries Inc. Domco rose 5.25 to 20.
Armstrong World Industries said on Monday that it offered to buy its Canadian rival for C$23 ($16.55) a share or C$488 million ($351 million).
It also said that it launched a lawsuit to prevent France's Sommer Allibert SA from merging its business, including 57 percent-owned Domco, with Germany's Tarkett AG.

Dairy firm Ault Foods Ltd. jumped 2.20 to 34.20 after its board said on Monday that it agreed to a C$34 ($24.48) a share or C$415 million ($299 million) white knight takeover bid by Italy's Parmalat Finanziaria SPA.
Privately held, Montreal-based Saputo Group, which has bid C$28 ($20.16) a share for Ault, said it did not rule out a higher bid.
